name: Why the process ended (exit reasons)
plain: Apps can read why they were killed: Android ApplicationExitInfo, iOS MetricKit exit metrics.
meaning: Lets apps and SDKs learn whether the system, the user or a crash ended a session. Android 17 adds a memory limiter reason; it also exposes behavior to the person's device.

android.persistence: Records kept for a short history (about the last 16 exits)
android.note: Reasons: REASON_LOW_MEMORY, REASON_USER_REQUESTED, REASON_EXCESSIVE_RESOURCE_USAGE, REASON_OTHER ('MemoryLimiter:AnonSwap' on 17)

ios.note: Counts foreground and background exits by reason, delivered about once per 24 h

limits.headline: Can learn why the system last ended the app, such as low memory
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens the next time the app starts or a report arrives
can: List recent reasons the app was ended on Android, such as low memory or you swiping it away
Get exit counts by reason on iPhone through MetricKit
Fix crashes and memory problems with the reports
cannot: Get iPhone reports faster than about once per 24 hours
limits.differs: Android lists recent exits one by one. iPhone gives counts about once a day.

story.what_it_is: An app can read why it was closed: by you, by a crash or by the system.

marketing.name: ApplicationExitInfo
marketing.pitch: Android tells apps why a previous process ended, such as a crash or low memory.

marketing.name: MetricKit
marketing.pitch: Apple reports crash and exit data to apps so they can fix problems.

story.for_you: You do not see it. When an app crashes or gets killed, it can learn why and later fix the bug. You may see fewer crashes over time.
story.for_makers: Makers use it to find crashes, out of memory kills and battery problems. It also shows how you use the phone. Patterns of exits can serve as a quiet device profile.

use_cases.example: A developer sees that many users hit a memory kill on one phone model and fixes it.
A game studio finds that a level crashes older phones and lowers its graphics.
A video app notes that the system closed it during long playback and reduces memory use.
A run tracker learns that the phone killed it mid run and starts a foreground service.
An analytics kit stores exit patterns to tell phones apart.
A security tool notices repeated kills that match a tampering attempt.

risks: Shows how you use the phone
story.android_note: Android 17 adds a memory limiter reason to ApplicationExitInfo.
story.ios_note: iPhone reports exit data in aggregate through MetricKit.

history.change: App memory limits report REASON_OTHER with MemoryLimiter:AnonSwap
